newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bosnian Serb refinery reopens with Yugo help-paper.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb refinery reopens with Yugo help-paper.

text.p: Bosnian Serbs have reopened their major oil refinery in Srpski Brod, after almost six years of closure due to war, Belgrade papers reported on Wednesday.
The Srpski Brod refinery, belonging to Energoinvest, will process between 1,500 and 1,800 tonnes of crude a day, far below its pre-war daily output of 9,000 tonnes.

"The opening of the refinery is the first step in the revival of the economy of the Bosnian Serb republic and the first big result of a special ties agreement signed with Yugoslavia," Momcilo Krajisnik, Serb member of Bosnia's collective presidency, was quoted as saying.
Krajisnik thanked Serbian oil industry Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS) for supplying oil to start the refinery.
Yugoslavia's NIS Jugopetrol provided 20,000 tonnes of crude to the Srpski Brod refinery, the refinery director Vojin Mijucic said.

Mijucic said the refinery needed around $100 million in fresh investment to return in full to its pre-war capacities or $50 million if it were to operate without its accompanying infrastructure -- warehouses, pipelines etc.

Energoinvest was looking at Russia and former Soviet republics for possible partners, but before clinching any partnership deal the refinery needed to undergo ownership transformation, Mijucic said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 43 05
